# XCMP Resource Admission And Outbound Capacity Backports

This is the published Apache-2.0 `cumulus-pallet-xcmp-queue 0.35.0` from the selected stable2609-1 dependency line, applied through the existing root `[patch.crates-io]` mechanism. The original crate checksum is `e9d07c06494fb9ca7fc40c7c424f8d60a2f27d91f270a1328c506b3378725470`; its published VCS identity is `paritytech/polkadot-sdk` commit `404083bd86004d7956ce36763726a6f2c7a2b99a` at `cumulus/pallets/xcmp-queue`. The original `src/lib.rs` SHA256 is `be6bcbcadde83a237ac167d9a5e294da664dea58ce50858715365dfbb01e6fef`, and `src/weights_ext.rs` is `4b72177982524144ff65022f952d890d79d51753326573ba650c33fd66611956`.

## Admission Changes

- Decoder entry charges its base and checks remaining capacity against the complete remaining encoded stream before decoding. Actual counted bytes settle inside that admitted upper bound, including decoder errors. This requires monotone byte-domain WeightInfo; physical validity of the inherited benchmark/caller units remains a separate gate. The bound is conservative: an affordable next XCM may refuse when its remaining concatenated suffix does not fit. Wire-format support and tested sufficiently funded ordering are preserved; universal finite-budget prefix acceptance is not claimed. `admission_remaining_stream_bound_is_conservative` makes this trade-off executable.
- Hosts provide `Config::MaxInboundPageSize`, the inbound queue heap-position bound including item headers. An empty ready footprint must imply no persisted append tail. It is not the outbound HRMP page limit. DEOS's Message Queue satisfies that contract through its begin/end indexes and binds the existing HeapSize without a new consensus storage item or context restriction.
- Initialization pays metadata bootstrap, inspects the bounded queue footprint, and prepays original-tail discovery/rewrite at the declared page bound before admitting the sender to one invocation-local cache. Its Boolean retains one prepaid first access through empty or failed decode packets. Failed initialization grants no warm authority.
- Later page accesses prepay the same bounded RefTime owner without another original-page proof charge. Publication charges only the non-position owner, avoiding duplicate page accounting. An unaffordable zero-message candidate performs no publication or callback; empty input remains a metadata-only benchmark operation.
- Bootstrap/decode capacity refusals return normally. Neither caught panics nor a clamped return implements admission. Checked meter operations retain admitted charges; transaction rollback does not make diagnostic incurred work zero.

## Outbound Notification Capacity

The separate outbound correction backports the user-authored [upstream PR #13816](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/pull/13816), reviewed head `86c61681b51ad10e2822a5de09e71382fa030a95`. Read-only GitHub inspection on 2026-11-12 confirmed the PR remains open and unmerged at that head. The production change is the same four-line guard: the complete encoded opaque capability notification must fit `max_size_now` before marking notification-sent or exporting its page. Insufficient byte capacity retains eligibility for recovery; exact-fit capacity is accepted. This does not change inbound admission, decoder pricing, generated weights, dependency versions or the SDK graph.

`opaque_notification_respects_channel_capacity` adapts the reviewed upstream regression to this pinned SDK by using the existing `status_for` storage lookup instead of the newer upstream test helper. Peer `1000` delegates to real Parachain System channel status, not the unlimited `HRMP_PARA_ID` mock. Three fresh-state cases cover zero free bytes with an available count slot, exact-fit bytes, and full message count with spare bytes; each checks export/sent eligibility, capacity recovery and absence of duplicate notifications.

Before the guard, the selected regression ran one test and failed on zero-byte capacity, exporting `[(1000, [3])]` and marking sent. With the guard, the standalone default-feature route below passed all 41 unit tests, including the three-case regression and existing inbound admission controls; zero doctests were selected. Native package conformance is not runtime artifact acceptance or physical decoder-price qualification.

## Scope And Validation

Generated `weights.rs` coefficients remain byte-identical to the published package. The new composition and host bound establish source-level admission against that model, not qualified production RefTime, complete state-witness coverage, whole context ownership, quarter compliance or artifact equivalence. Opaque-format metadata, signals, complete input/hash/callback work and host root/import/commit/rollback remain in the existing enclosing qualification gate.

`opaque_capability_notice_precedes_unfunded_enqueue_refusal` is an executable qualification obstruction, not admission acceptance. Header-only, valid-message and malformed-length opaque packets each insert the sender's outbound capability status under a zero internal allowance, return zero Weight and publish no message. Negotiation precedes cold-bootstrap refusal, so neither that refused bootstrap nor the decoder/page/publication owners cover the status access. The existing enclosing context owner must qualify this bounded status read/search/insert/rewrite and its refusal/input work exactly once before a zero handler return can support complete accounting. Moving negotiation behind bootstrap would change header-only negotiation semantics without supplying its missing price; no such production change is made.

Runtime regressions use `SKIP_WASM_BUILD=1 ./scripts/ci-local.sh --only tests --package deos-runtime --test-filter tests::actors_integration_tests::xcmp_`, separately with `--release`. They execute real handler/context/queue paths, exact and one-unit-short capacity, funded cold/warm reuse, original refusal operands, empty-candidate refusal and root/prior-MQ restoration. The existing stored-context consumer separately checks the now-controlled debug refusal. Original counterexamples and source/binary identities remain in the existing assurance owner.

`src/tests.rs` contains upstream-style decoder and failed-bootstrap regressions; published dev dependencies are restored at the selected versions in the normalized manifest. The vendored dependency owns a separate library-test workspace/lock without becoming a lockstep DEOS workspace member. Run `SKIP_WASM_BUILD=1 ./scripts/ci-local.sh --only tests --package cumulus-pallet-xcmp-queue --manifest-path template/vendor/cumulus-pallet-xcmp-queue/Cargo.toml` from the repository root; optional `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` may reuse the project target directory. The standalone lock is an upstream-style dev profile, not the DEOS production graph or a physical transfer attestation. The ordinary root `--package` route alone cannot test a nonmember's dev dependencies. Port these regressions and the host-bound binding with an upstream submission; no external PR/publication is performed here.

All other source modules retain their published bytes. `src/lib.rs`, `weights_ext.rs`, `mock.rs` and `tests.rs` carry the bounded admission/host/test changes. This source patch does not update the separately downloaded Omni Node, generate Weight or issue production Wasm/metadata. The [existing integration owner](../../../docs/deos/actors.integration.en.md#conservative-fixed-owner-composition) owns DEOS composition and release applicability.
